messages:
sam: Quick sync — I pushed a tiny prototype of a 'safety fallback chooser' in the console. Want opinions on what modes we should surface and how to show triggers + audit history.
elaine: Nice. Can you paste the minimal config you're imagining? UI needs to be tiny for PMs.
sam: Sure, rough example we used in the mock:
```yaml
modes:
  - passthrough
  - latency-degrade
  - quality-degrade
triggers:
  - error_rate > 1.5% over 1m
  - p95 latency > 600ms
audit: true
sampling: 10%
```
joel: Two quick asks: show estimated cost/latency delta per mode, and make the chosen mode explainable (why it fired). Otherwise SREs will ignore it.
priya: +1 on the explainability. Also audit logs need immutable events with user id + config diff. We should store files in the same retention bucket as rollout traces.
sam: Good. Thinking console flow: choose mode, scope (route/model/tag), triggers (preset or custom), then preview (simulate on last N minutes), then commit. Preview should show a simulated traffic histogram and example responses.
elaine: Simulation is huge — can we reuse existing replay infra? Otherwise cost to run previews will be high.
joel: We can reuse the playback infra but need to wire in KV-caching emulation (prefix caching changes results). If we can't emulate caches, preview might overstate latency. Add a cache toggle.
priya: Also add a "no-audit" checkbox only for dev routes (explicitly disallowed for production). Legal asked for that guard.
karen: UX nit: when a trigger fires, show a small inline card with the cause + "what will happen" (one-liner) and an affordance to roll back to the previous mode. Users hate hunting in the rollout timeline.
sam: Rollback button + automatic rollback TTL sounds right. We should let teams opt into auto-rollback after X minutes if error rate drops below threshold.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] simulation job queued (job id=sim-5421)
elaine: For telemetry: we need token-level breakdown (cost) and per-route failure taxonomy. The current route dashboard lumps all errors — categorize by upstream vs model vs infra.
joel: Agree. Also expose the signal that triggered the fallback in tracing spans: fallback.trigger.reason and fallback.simulated.effect. That will simplify alerts.
priya: On audit retention: default 90 days, enterprise option 1y. We must include redaction metadata for prompts. Audit entries: who changed, config diff, preview snapshot (sample responses), and a compact event digest for quick search.
sam: How should we present the modes? Simple radio with short descriptions, or an editor for advanced users?
karen: Radio with "advanced" link that expands config. Keep main path low friction.
elaine: One more: sampling. For noisy signals (traffic spikes) preview and audits should sample deterministically (seeded by route+day) so replay is stable.
joel: Edge case: oscillation — if fallback frequently toggles on/off we need hysteresis or a cool-down. Let's add a "min duration" and "cooldown" fields to prevent noisy flaps.
priya: Also need a policy for quota accounting when a fallback routes to a higher-cost model — teams must opt into cross-model spend or we auto-throttle. Show a clear banner if quota impact > 10%.
sam: Good call. I'll add a banner mock that shows estimated spend delta and a checkbox to allow temporary budget override.
ops-bot: [audit-bot] new audit bucket created: rollouts-prod-logs-2024. (automated)
karen: Can we add an "explainability" link that opens an anonymized example pair: original response vs fallback response + short note why fallback improved availability but maybe lowered quality. Helpful for product folks.
sam: Love that. Action items: 1) joel to add cache toggle to preview + hysteresis fields to the config. 2) priya to draft audit schema (diff, sample, redaction flags). 3) elaine/karen to wire the simple/advanced UX and banner copy. I'll update the prototype and re-upload.
joel: I'll PR a preview job patch this afternoon.
priya: Drafting audit schema now, will post link when done.
sam: Thanks all — will push updated mock in ~2 hours. Ping me if you want a quick screen share to walk through simulation. :thumbsup:
